glyphs.label: WebCrypto
glyphs.description: SubtleCrypto lives in the browser — a chrome window with a small key signals Web API crypto (genkey, digest, AEAD, KDF, …).

glyphs.label: OpenPGP
glyphs.description: ModernPGP convention for encrypted mail/messages — flap envelope with lock-shackle (gpg.encrypt, gpg.sign, …).

glyphs.label: age
glyphs.description: age encrypts files, not messages — a page with a folded corner and a shackle, distinguishing it from OpenPGP's envelope (age.keygen, age.encrypt, …).

glyphs.label: agent.decrypt
glyphs.metaphor: Vault wall with two text lines emerging
glyphs.description: Plaintext out, wall closed. Distinct from gpg-decrypt's open shackle: nothing here opens.

glyphs.label: agent.sign
glyphs.metaphor: Vault wall with a quill stroke emerging through a gap
glyphs.description: The signature leaves, the key does not — the vault outline opens on the right just far enough for the sign quill to pass through.

glyphs.label: Boundary
glyphs.metaphor: Vault wall with a keyhole inside it
glyphs.description: The wall is the subject: a rounded vault outline with the keyhole centred inside, for ops that use a key without letting it out (agent.sign, agent.decrypt).

glyphs.label: SSH
glyphs.metaphor: Terminal prompt chevron with a key on the baseline
glyphs.description: The shell's key — a prompt chevron with a horizontal key lying to its right. No window chrome, distinguishing it from WebCrypto's browser-plus-key (ssh.encode, ssh.sign, …).

glyphs.label: Keys & wire
glyphs.metaphor: Key whose shank trails into three linked blocks
glyphs.description: The RFC 4253 blob is literally a chain of length-prefixed fields — a key head trailing chained blocks reads as 'wire format' at 20px (ssh.encode, ssh.decode, ssh.fingerprint).

glyphs.label: sshsig
glyphs.metaphor: Quill stroke with a prompt chevron tucked lower-left
glyphs.description: The established signature quill, marked as the shell's — sshsig format, what ssh-keygen -Y and git SSH signing produce (ssh.sign, ssh.verify).

glyphs.label: Encoding
glyphs.description: Bytes ↔ text transforms (pem, base64, hex, …) — folded rails with encode/decode arrowheads.

glyphs.label: Input / output
glyphs.description: Runtime ports and tiles (input, out, random, qr) — a simple content panel.

glyphs.label: Flow
glyphs.description: Pipeline control (foreach, tee, in, as) — two L-shaped forks suggesting stem/branch flow.

glyphs.label: Agent
glyphs.description: The Agent toolbox and the vault shelf: a key is used inside, and never comes out. The keyhole is the mark `agent-boundary`, `agent-decrypt` and `agent-sign` already carry inside their vault wall, drawn here on its own and large — the toolbox is the keyhole, the shelf is the keyhole put behind a wall, so the two differ by a whole silhouette (round-with-a-skirt against square) rather than by a detail. It replaces a key crossed by an r=5.5 TTL arc that was unreadable at both shipping sizes: rasterised at 12px the old bow region held 3.73 of ink with one clear pixel in sixteen, against 0.36 and four for this ring. TTL is not what separates the agent from Keys — that the key stays inside is, and that is what a keyhole says.

glyphs.label: HKP
glyphs.description: HTTP Keyserver Protocol lookup/search — a central node with compass spokes (directory + fetch).

glyphs.label: SSS / BLIP39
glyphs.description: Shamir secret sharing / BLIP39 — offset stacked cards as K-of-N fragments (any threshold recovers; a single share is useless alone).

glyphs.label: WebAuthn
glyphs.description: Official passkey layout: person on the left, simplified key on the right slightly overlapping (create, prf, caps).
refs: FIDO Alliance Passkey Icon Usage Guidelines

glyphs.label: OTP
glyphs.metaphor: Key whose bow is a countdown dial
glyphs.description: A TOTP secret is a key that expires. The shank is the `password` shelf glyph's, because the shared secret underneath is the same kind of thing; the bow is a dial with hands and a gap at twelve where the period has run off. Two cues rather than one on purpose — at 16px the gap alone reads as a broken circle and the hands alone read as a plain clock, and it has to stay distinct from `password` right beside it in the drawer.

glyphs.label: Keys
glyphs.metaphor: Key, bow hollow, teeth up the shank
glyphs.description: WebCrypto key material — genkey, export, import; the base drawing for `genkey`, `gpg-genkey` and `passphrase`. The bow is a plain ring rather than the old outlined silhouette with an r=1 hole punched in it: at 12px that hole filled solid, and the silhouette's closing chord ran straight through the bow, so the whole thing read as a diagonal lozenge. Measured in a 4x4 window on the bow centre at 12px the old drawing carried 1.89 of ink, where `key-public` carries 0 and the deliberately filled `key-secret` carries 4 — it sat halfway into the range the sensitivity split reserves. This one measures 0, four clear pixels of four, the same as `key-public`. It runs bow-low to teeth-high so it cannot be read as `inspect`'s magnifier, whose handle falls the other way, and stays off the horizontal axis `password` and the `key-*` kind badges use.

glyphs.label: Digest
glyphs.metaphor: Input lines collapsing into hash bars
glyphs.description: Cryptographic hash — long input lines beside a “#”-like pair of bars (digest).

glyphs.label: Sign
glyphs.description: Digital signature — a pen tip stroke (WebCrypto sign/verify or OpenPGP gpgsign shelf).

glyphs.label: AEAD
glyphs.description: Authenticated encryption (AES-GCM) — protective shield.

glyphs.label: Cipher
glyphs.description: Unauthenticated block/stream ciphers (AES-CBC/CTR) — four cells with a swap diagonal (not an “eye”).

glyphs.label: RSA
glyphs.description: RSA-OAEP / PKCS1 ops — document lines plus a small key.

glyphs.label: KDF
glyphs.description: HKDF/PBKDF2 — narrow extract phase then widen expand (RFC 5869 extract-then-expand).

glyphs.label: Agreement
glyphs.description: ECDH / X25519 — two key heads meeting at a shared vertical (shared secret).

glyphs.label: Wrap
glyphs.description: Key wrap / unwrap — 3D parcel with ribbon crease.

glyphs.label: Public key
glyphs.description: OpenPGP public-key ops (genkey, encrypt, inspect) — message envelope under a head.

glyphs.label: Password
glyphs.description: Symmetric OpenPGP password/SKESK shelf — key bow and bit.

glyphs.label: Split
glyphs.description: SSS split / BLIP39 encode — energy splitting into branches.

glyphs.label: Combine
glyphs.description: SSS combine — signal converging toward recovery, with a small refresh corner.

glyphs.label: Binary
glyphs.description: Binary encodings shelf — a 2×2 bit grid (fallback when a tool has no dedicated glyph).

glyphs.label: Hex
glyphs.description: `to hex` / `from hex` — hexagon (hex) with a center cross (byte grid).

glyphs.label: Base64
glyphs.description: Base64 / Base64url — two full code rows and a truncated third with twin hash marks.

glyphs.label: Base32
glyphs.description: Base32 — three encoding rows with a small expand chevron (5-bit alphabet).

glyphs.label: PEM
glyphs.description: PEM / DER armor — framed document with BEGIN/END-style text lines.

glyphs.label: Text
glyphs.description: Text encodings (utf8) — a capital T with baseline marks.

glyphs.label: Ports
glyphs.description: I/O ports — two sockets with a bridge (input/out/random).

glyphs.label: Files
glyphs.description: Whole-file operations (age.encrypt, stream.seal) — a page rather than the AEAD shield, because these produce a framed file with many tags, not one message with one.

glyphs.label: Control
glyphs.description: Flow control shelf — three nodes linked by a U-shaped bus.

glyphs.label: Essentials
glyphs.description: WebAuthn essentials (caps, create, prf) — passkey person plus a readiness checkmark.

glyphs.label: Attestation / MDS
glyphs.description: Soft attestation / FIDO MDS — shield containing a checkmark.

glyphs.label: Directory
glyphs.description: HKP directory search — two contact silhouettes (alias of recipients).

glyphs.label: Recipients
glyphs.description: Recipients list / merge — two contact silhouettes.

glyphs.label: Variables / slots
glyphs.description: Kernel @slots chip — three cells and a plus for binding live values.

glyphs.label: Preferences
glyphs.description: Settings / preferences control.

glyphs.label: More
glyphs.description: Overflow / more menu.

glyphs.label: Keyboard shortcuts
glyphs.description: Keyboard shortcuts help — simple keyboard outline with keys.

glyphs.label: Fingerprint
glyphs.description: OpenPGP key fingerprint — ridge arcs (ModernPGP fingerprint icon).

glyphs.label: Unlock
glyphs.description: Unlock vault key into session — shackle open.

glyphs.label: Lock
glyphs.description: Lock / clear session material — shackle closed.

glyphs.label: Generate key
glyphs.description: WebCrypto genkey — the `keys` key with a plus in the free lower-right quadrant, the same 'and one more' mark `agent-list` and `wa-get` use. The old spark rays were three 1.2-unit ticks, 0.7px of noise at 12px beside a bow that had already filled in.

glyphs.label: Export
glyphs.description: Export key material — upload arrow from tray.

glyphs.label: Import
glyphs.description: Import key material — download arrow into tray.

glyphs.label: Random
glyphs.description: CSPRNG random bytes — irregular bit cells.

glyphs.label: Input
glyphs.description: Runtime input — content panel pushed right, with a full arrow (shaft and head) crossing its left edge. The old inbound mark was a bare 4-unit rail, which left `input` and `out` differing by which side a nub sat on.

glyphs.label: Out
glyphs.description: Emit / slot out — the conjugate of `input`: panel pushed left, full arrow leaving the right edge. Direction is carried by an arrowhead that survives 12px, not by the side a rail sits on.

glyphs.label: Passphrase
glyphs.description: Passphrase source (io / ports) — the `keys` key, lifted and shortened, over a full-width text baseline: a secret that is typed. The old drawing's bow was an open arc that never closed, so it read as a hook over a line; this bow measures 0.11 of ink in the 4x4 bow window at 12px against the old 2.79, four clear pixels against none.

glyphs.label: Clipboard
glyphs.description: Clipboard source/sink - board with binder clip (clipboard.read, clipboard.write).

glyphs.label: File read
glyphs.description: file.read - a document on disk feeding the pipeline; the arrow leaves the page because bytes flow out of the file.

glyphs.label: File save
glyphs.description: file.save - the pipeline value coming to rest on disk; down is the universal save direction.

glyphs.label: Chunked AEAD
glyphs.metaphor: Three sealed blocks in a row
glyphs.description: stream.seal / stream.open - a file split into independently-tagged chunks, each with its own shackle, which is exactly what the STREAM construction does.

glyphs.label: age identity
glyphs.description: age.keygen / age.recipient - an X25519 identity and the recipient derived from it.

glyphs.label: age file
glyphs.description: age.encrypt / age.decrypt - a padlocked age-encryption.org/v1 file.

glyphs.label: QR
glyphs.description: QR code sink — three finder patterns plus modules.

glyphs.label: Inspect
glyphs.description: Inspect / dump — a plain magnifier, lens enlarged to r=5 and the crosshair dropped. The cross was the detail that made this and `hkp-search` the same drawing described twice; the magnifier stays here because inspect is the generic 'look at this', and `hkp-search` now says what it looks through.

glyphs.label: Peek
glyphs.description: Peek side snapshot — eye outline.

glyphs.label: Text sink
glyphs.description: text / print sink — a typographic T whose stem carries an arrowhead down onto a floor line. The old outbound tick was a 2-unit stroke invisible at 12px, which left this and the `text` encoding glyph as the same drawing; the arrow and the floor are a silhouette apart from it.

glyphs.label: Foreach
glyphs.description: foreach — three tiles suggesting map-over-items.

glyphs.label: Tee
glyphs.description: tee — stem with left/right branch forks.

glyphs.label: In
glyphs.description: in @slot — arrow into a vertical slot rail.

glyphs.label: As
glyphs.description: as cast — A-shaped chevron over a baseline.

glyphs.label: Select
glyphs.description: select / .public — folded document page.

glyphs.label: At
glyphs.description: at / [n] index — @-like spiral.

glyphs.label: OpenPGP encrypt
glyphs.description: gpg.encrypt — a padlock whose body is solid, because what it produces is opaque. Filled rather than a finer mark: `age-lock` is already a closed hollow padlock on age.encrypt, and at 12px this carries 41.6 of ink against its 28.3, a 1.47x difference no detail at this size could match. Its conjugate `gpg-decrypt` is the same body hollow with the shackle open, so the pair reads as one act in two directions.

glyphs.label: OpenPGP sign
glyphs.description: gpg.sign / gpg.verify — pen tip stroke.

glyphs.label: OpenPGP genkey
glyphs.description: gpg.genkey — the `keys` key under a single bold armour bar, top left, where the key leaves the box empty. One 6-unit rule rather than the old 4x1.5 block, which at 12px was a 2.4x0.9px nub. Position as well as shape separates it from `genkey`: bar high left against plus low right.

glyphs.label: OpenPGP inspect
glyphs.description: gpg.inspect — message panel with lens.

glyphs.label: OpenPGP symmetric
glyphs.description: gpg.symencrypt / gpg.symdecrypt — passphrase key under a panel.

glyphs.label: BLIP39
glyphs.description: blip39 — stacked word rows for share mnemonics.

glyphs.label: Shares
glyphs.description: shares input — stacked offset cards.

glyphs.label: Agent list
glyphs.description: agent.list — list lines with a plus mark.

glyphs.label: Agent save
glyphs.description: agent.save — save card with top flap.

glyphs.label: HKP search
glyphs.description: hkp.search — a keyserver listing with a lens over it. Searching a directory is not the same act as inspecting a value, and drawing the directory is what separates it from `inspect`: two full-width rules give it a rectangular mass at the top that a bare magnifier has nowhere, 25.2 of ink at 12px against 19.1.

glyphs.label: HKP get
glyphs.description: hkp.get — arrow down to baseline.

glyphs.label: HKP filter
glyphs.description: hkp.filter — funnel / filter shape.

glyphs.label: HKP cache
glyphs.description: hkp.cache — a folder, not a panel. Its old drawing was a bordered panel with a small tab, one of four panels in the drawer separated by a unit or two of interior mark; the folder's stepped top edge is a silhouette difference instead.

glyphs.label: HKDF
glyphs.description: hkdf — extract rectangle feeding an expand fan.

glyphs.label: PBKDF2
glyphs.description: pbkdf2 — password key under an extract panel.

glyphs.label: WebAuthn create
glyphs.description: webauthn.create — person plus overlapping key.

glyphs.label: WebAuthn get
glyphs.description: webauthn.get — person plus downward arrow.

glyphs.label: WebAuthn PRF
glyphs.description: webauthn.prf — person plus digest bars.

glyphs.label: WebAuthn caps
glyphs.description: webauthn.caps — person plus readiness check.

glyphs.label: WebAuthn attest
glyphs.description: webauthn.attest — attestation shield.

glyphs.label: WebAuthn MDS
glyphs.description: webauthn.mds — MDS document with lens.

glyphs.label: JOSE
glyphs.description: A compact JOSE serialization is header.payload.signature - three blocks with the separators between them, plus the signature spark (jose.sign, jose.verify).

glyphs.label: JWE envelope
glyphs.metaphor: Token whose middle segment is filled
glyphs.description: A JWE carries an encrypted payload rather than a signed one, so it is the `jose` token with the payload segment blacked out — the part you cannot read. Segment ink at 12px is 5.89 against `jose`'s 2.58, a 2.28x difference. It was an envelope with a lock shackle, which at badge size was the same silhouette as `pubkey` and `openpgp`; staying inside the JOSE token family says more, and says it at 12px.

glyphs.label: Decode token
glyphs.description: Reading a token without verifying it - the three segments with an inspection lens, deliberately not the signature spark (jose.decode).

glyphs.label: OpenPGP decrypt
glyphs.description: gpg.decrypt — the conjugate of `gpg-encrypt`: same square body, hollow, shackle swung open. The shackle hinges on the right and opens left, the mirror of `unlock`, which is the only other open padlock the drawer renders; the square body keeps both off `lock` / `age-lock`, which are round-cornered.

glyphs.label: Encode
glyphs.description: Forward direction of a conjugate pair - encode, wrap, sign.

glyphs.label: Decode
glyphs.description: Reverse direction of a conjugate pair - decode, unwrap, verify. Mirrors encode exactly so direction reads without labels.

glyphs.label: Public key
glyphs.description: The unmarked member of the sensitivity pair: an ordinary key, bow hollow. You can see through it, because there is nothing in it to hide. Identical to key-secret in every other respect - same bow radius, same shank, same two bits - so the one thing that differs is the one thing that matters.

glyphs.label: Secret key
glyphs.description: The same key as key-public with its bow filled in: solid, opaque, something inside. Fill rather than a second mark because the badge renders at 12-16px, where a gap, a dot or an extra tooth all close up - at 12px a rasterised disc against a rasterised ring is still unmistakable, which no finer cue survives. This is the shape channel that carries the sensitivity split beside the badge tint, so a reader who cannot separate the two hues still can.

glyphs.label: Keypair
glyphs.metaphor: Two bows on one shank, one filled and one hollow
glyphs.description: Both halves on a single key: the filled bow is the secret one, the hollow bow the public one. It reads on the secret side of the split because a filled bow is present, which is the honest claim - a keypair holds secret material even though its identity is showable.

glyphs.label: WebRTC
glyphs.description: A connection is a span the two ends stand on: an arch between two solid footings. Not a wire — ICE builds the route, it is not handed one. Distinct from ports (two sockets bridged, the ICE/STUN shelf) because the mass sits in the footings rather than the band.

glyphs.label: Peer & signaling
glyphs.metaphor: Offer and answer facing each other
glyphs.description: Two solid wedges pointed at one another across a gap — the offer and the answer, not yet met. Signalling is exactly the part where the two halves are addressed to each other and have not arrived (quorum.offer/join/close, rtc.offer/answer/state/restart).

glyphs.label: Data channel
glyphs.description: An RTCDataChannel is bidirectional and both directions are the users job: an up arrow and a down arrow side by side (quorum.send, quorum.recv, peer.send, peer.recv, rtc.stats). Vertical on purpose — the horizontal band belongs to ports.
